name: comp-similar -- the functional-overlap axis: BM25 similarity over a resource's SUMMARY (not its name) + the superseded-twin decommission heuristic that ties the comp-debris/heat/dups/drift family into one usable decommission workflow
description: Andrew-direct (0.8.0_AE_CloudComp terminal, 2026-07-17; verbatim recorded @dc4207c7c / 1d81e760b / 3d326af47). A new comp-tool AND the doctrine + usage playbook around it, scoped explicitly by Andrew as three things in one: the WHY (why a functional-similarity tool exists and how deprecated/overlapping resources confuse agents), the HOW (how to USE comp-similar together with comp-dups/comp-debris/comp-heat/comp-drift to find decommission candidates), and the WHAT (the infrastructure). comp-similar scores BM25 lexical similarity over a resource's SUMMARY (what it DOES) where comp-dups scores over its name/file-body (what it IS/is-made-of) -- the functional-overlap axis the decommission family lacks. Headline mode = Andrew's superseded-twin fast-scan: a decommission candidate = a similar-name cluster with VERY HIGH summary similarity AND a LARGE hot-vs-cold heat divergence (one resource quietly replaced another, the old left running). Engine = the existing dup_scan.py BM25 class (copy-reuse, Andrew's stated intent). The one novel substrate = a STABLE resource-summary corpus: a new ARN-keyed append-only Iceberg table resource_summaries in the globgrph Nessie catalog (NOT a graph_nodes column -- that table is derived+regenerated+clobbered), projected into Kuzu as a node `summary` property via LEFT-JOIN so a re-derive never clobbers the editorial overlay. v1 corpus = derive-at-scan from the graph neighborhood (pipescript-style projection, uniform across resource types, no producer change); the authored one-off pass (~549 prime targets of ~841 independent resources / 1,894 ARN-bearing) is the enrichment. Advisory, never deletes, hold-aware -- same discipline as comp-dups + comp-debris. Disposal stays OPAL_LCLRPO's CTO-gated Andrew-delete-word path (no second disposal path).
